findings.title: Zip-Slip path traversal in BitsZip.extract(): ZipEntry names used unsanitized as output paths
findings.code_excerpt: final BufferedOutputStream out = new BufferedOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(new File(outDir,name)));
findings.entry_point: Any zip archive passed as the zipFile argument of BitsZip.extract(String zipFile, String outDir); attacker controls every ZipEntry name (entry.getName() at line 75)
findings.sink: new File(outDir, name) -> FileOutputStream at line 44 (also mkdirs at lines 77 and 86-88)
findings.data_path: extract() line 74 iterates zin.getNextEntry(); line 75 name = entry.getName(); line 84 dirPart(name) only splits on File.separatorChar (never checks '..' or leading '/'); line 92 calls extractFile(zin, outDir, name) which opens new File(outDir,name) at line 44 and copies entry bytes into it
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker crafts a level/update pack zip containing an entry named '../../files/sharedprefs/game.xml' (or an absolute path). When a game variant extracts the pack, bytes are written outside outDir to any path the app UID can write: private files dir, shared_preferences XMLs (flip 'paid=true', alter saved progress), or the executable-adjacent data of the app. This persists tampering across restarts and can corrupt or forge other apps'-visible state on old, shared external storage.
findings.preconditions: Within THIS repository there is no caller: grep shows BitsZip.extract is referenced nowhere except its own definition, so exploitation requires a sibling BitsEngine-based game variant that routes a downloaded/user-supplied zip (e.g. a level pack from the apo-games.de infrastructure present in other variants) into this public static API. Java's ZipInputStream does not sanitize '../' in entry names, so no runtime guard exists.
findings.validation_plan: Build a tiny Android harness linking this engine source; create a zip whose entry is named '../../databases/test_evil.db' plus filler content; call BitsZip.extract(zipPath, context.getExternalFilesDir(null).getAbsolutePath()) ; observe that /data/data/<pkg>/databases/test_evil.db now exists outside the intended outDir while logcat shows only success (return true). Repeat with an absolute-path entry ('/data/local/tmp/x') to confirm second variant.

findings.title: Attacker-readable file bytes passed straight into native libmodplug parser (ModPlug_JLoad)
findings.code_excerpt: this.mMODPlayer.LoadMODData( buffer );  // buffer = whole file read at lines 86-88
findings.entry_point: BitsMusicPlayer.getInstance().play(String file, ...) with any '.xm' (actually any module-format) path; the file content is fully attacker-controllable if it lives in public storage (getExternalStorageDirectory()/BitsEngine-Game per BitsIO.java:57 and BitsApp.java:115)
findings.sink: native boolean ModPlug_JLoad(byte[] buffer, int size) declared in _from_jar_andmodplug-1.0/com/peculiargames/andmodplug/PlayerThread.java:878, invoked from PlayerThread.LoadMODData at PlayerThread.java:406; parsing happens inside C library libmodplug
findings.data_path: play(file,...) (BitsMusicPlayer.java:201 detects '.xm') -> play(...) private overload line 262-264 -> load() line 82-90: FileInputStream(mFile) -> byte[] buffer -> MODResourcePlayer.LoadMODData(buffer) (MODResourcePlayer.java extends PlayerThread) -> ModPlug_JLoad(modData, modData.length) crosses JNI into libmodplug's loader. The comment at BitsMusicPlayer.java:201 ('TODO kann noch mehr als nur XM!!!') confirms more formats than XM reach the native loader.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker supplies a malicious module file (classic libmodplug CVE families: OOB reads/writes in S3M/IT/MOD loaders) named song.xm in the shared folder /sdcard/BitsEngine-Game/. Victim plays the track; malformed structures hit C code with no bounds checking, yielding native memory corruption -> crash at minimum, potential code execution in-process with the game's permissions.
findings.preconditions: No in-repo caller invokes BitsMusicPlayer.play with an untrusted path in this variant (only resetInstance/stop are called, BitsGame.java:202, BitsApp.java:465). Reachable only in sibling game variants that pass a user-writable/downloaded music file. Also requires libmodplug-<VERS>.so to be the historical vulnerable versions (source of the .so is not in this repo, only the JNI stub).
findings.validation_plan: In an engine test app call BitsMusicPlayer.getInstance().play('/sdcard/BitsEngine-Game/craft.xm', pitch=1, volume=1, loop=false) with a known libmodplug crasher input (e.g. a truncated/oversized instrument-count IT file from an ASAN libmodplug PoC); observe SIGSEGV with libmodplug.so frames in the tombstone (adb bugreport). A clean parse of a valid .xm serves as negative control.

findings.title: Unescaped caller string concatenated into regex in BitsIO.findFile (crash / ReDoS)
findings.code_excerpt: if( files[i].matches("(?i)^" + file + ".*$") == true ) { //will ignore the case; looks for
findings.entry_point: The file parameter of BitsIO.findFile(String path, String file, boolean isPrefix) when isPrefix=true; if a sibling variant ever derives this argument from user content (level name, filename typed in UI, downloaded listing) it becomes attacker-controlled
findings.sink: String.matches() compiles the concatenation '(?i)^'+file+'.*$' with java.util.regex.Pattern on the calling thread (game thread)
findings.data_path: caller -> findFile() line 147 branch isPrefix==true -> line 148 files[i].matches("(?i)^" + file + ".*$") executed once per entry returned by f.list() at line 145, amplifying backtracking cost by directory size
findings.attack_scenario: Two modes: (a) crash - a syntactically invalid pattern fragment such as 'a{{' throws PatternSyntaxException on every loop iteration, killing the game thread; (b) hang - a nested-quantifier pattern like '(a+)+$' matched against long filenames causes catastrophic backtracking, freezing the GL/logic thread (soft DoS). Both require no permissions beyond making findFile receive the crafted string.
findings.preconditions: findFile has no caller inside this variant (grep across all 98 files shows none); it is engine API. Impact additionally requires a game variant to feed untrusted text into the prefix argument and a directory containing matching-length filenames.
findings.validation_plan: Unit test on desktop JVM (same java.util.regex semantics): create temp dir with files 'aaaa...a' (200 chars x50 entries); call new BitsIO().findFile(dir, "(a+)+x", true) after relaxing visibility, measure wall time vs. benign prefix; then call with "a{{" and observe PatternSyntaxException stack trace originating at BitsIO.java:148.

categories_checked_and_absent: remote_code_loading - no ClassLoader.defineClass, DexClassLoader, URLClassLoader anywhere (grep over all 98 files); only getResourceAsStream for classpath bitmaps (BitsGLFactory.java:235)
insecure_transport - zero networking: no java.net/org.apache.http imports at all; every 'http://' hit is an Apache license header; there is no highscore/level-server code in this variant
untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream, Serializable readObject, Parcel deserialization of untrusted data

weak_integrity_check - MessageDigest/MD5 exists (BitsUtils.java:58,86) but is used ONLY for texture/audio pool deduplication (BitsGLFactory.java:273,904,946; BitsSoundFactory.java:170); no security decision depends on it, so no exploitable weakness
credential_or_secret_exposure - no keys, tokens, passwords, account data in tree

unsafe_custom_parser - XMI parser (BitsXmi2Mid.java:68-182) and MIDI reader (com.leff.midi) parse binary data but are uncalled in this variant and fail with Java exceptions (BufferUnderflowException), i.e. crash-only, no corruption; folded into notes rather than a finding
client_side_trust - no scores, unlocks, purchases or cheat-relevant logic exist in this engine-only variant
legacy_sandbox_assumption - no Applet/SecurityManager code; only a desktop remnant System.getProperty("user.dir") fallback in BitsIO.fileExists (BitsIO.java:178), harmless on Android

information_disclosure - BitsLog writes to logcat or a caller-chosen PrintStream (BitsLog.java:111,145-260) containing file paths; default TYPE_INFO and no in-repo setLogFileName call, so not elevated to a finding
notes: This variant is NOT a complete game: it is the 'BitsEngine' Android engine library (net.gliblybits.bitsengine, GliblyBits/Marc Wiedenhoeft, Apache-2.0) plus two vendored audio libraries (_from_jar_android-midi-libv3, _from_jar_andmodplug-1.0). There is no game screen logic, no highscore submission, no level download, hence the corpus-typical plain-HTTP apo-games.de traffic is genuinely ABSENT here (all 98 files swept). Because every dangerous primitive (BitsZip.extract, BitsIO.read/writePublicFile, BitsMusicPlayer.play) is exported engine API with no internal caller, findings 01-03 are latent: their reachability is inherited by whichever sibling game variants link this engine and feed it downloaded/user files - exactly the clone-and-own propagation this study measures. All three sinks live in shared infrastructure (BitsIO/BitsZip/BitsMusicPlayer + vendored jars), not game-specific code. Additional observations not rated as findings: (1) System.loadLibrary("modplug-"+VERS) at PlayerThread.java:912 loads a fixed bundled .so, not attacker-influenced; (2) BitsMusicPlayer.java:97 passes the file string to Uri.parse -> MediaPlayer.create, so a future caller passing an http:// URL would silently stream cleartext media; (3) BitsIO.writePublicFile/readPublicFile concatenate caller strings onto mPublicDir without canonicalization (BitsIO.java:423,430) - safe only as long as callers sanitize; (4) the repository layout embeds a stale absolute path as directories ('Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Android/BitsEngineAndroid/...'), indicating a misconfigured archive extraction; paths above cite it verbatim.
